subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.

spec.name: Alebrije Jaguar-Eagle
spec.description: A Oaxacan alebrije of painted wood: a jaguar-bodied, eagle-headed, eagle-winged beast with taloned hind feet and a feather-plumed tail, covered in dots, rosettes, flowers and zigzag bands in saturated colours.
spec.layout: Stands on four legs facing +Z, centred on x=0. Front to back: a hooked yellow eagle beak at z=+1.5, the head (centre z~0.95, y~1.4) on a thick S-curved neck rising from the chest (y~1.0, z~0.7), then a chunky jaguar torso (z -0.85..+0.85, centre y~0.88, belly y~0.55, back y~1.2) on short sturdy legs, then a tail curving back and upward ending in a fan of feather-flames at z~-2.0. The front legs are jaguar legs with big round paws. The hind legs have a fat feathered thigh over a bird-like hock and an eagle foot with 3 forward talons and 1 rear talon. The wings spread out from the shoulders (y~1.1) to x=+-1.7 in a display rest pose, raised a little (wrist y~1.45) with the feathers trailing backward (-Z) and fanning, the longest primaries at the tips. Proportions are chunky and toy-like: big head, thick neck, heavy shoulders, short legs, huge wings. Style: Oaxacan painted wood. Every surface is a flat bright colour broken up by small repeated parts: rows of white dots along every edge, rosette flowers (dark ring, coloured petals, gold centre dot), zigzag greca bands, leaf-and-vine scrolls, and stripes. Faceted low-poly forms with a slightly carved look. All motifs are small parts seated on the surfaces. Colours never blend; each stripe or dot is its own colour. Unpainted raw wood shows only at the toe tips and the horn-like beak ridge.

parts.builds: The jaguar torso as one loft over the hips, spine1, spine2 and chest joints (smooth skin), z -0.85..+0.85, about 0.62 wide at the chest and hips and a bit narrower at the waist, 0.55..0.7 tall, deep chest and a rounded rump. Colouring: jaguarOrange back, a cream belly band along the underside (use sectors or a separate belly loft), and a marigold stripe low on the flanks. Jaguar markings as small parts seated on the surface with surface.scatter or along: about 30 rosettes (a ring of 5 small indigo spheres or flat discs around a gold or magenta centre dot) over the back and flanks, plus single indigo spots on the haunches. Painted-wood folk decoration: a magenta saddle strip down the spine with a turquoise zigzag (greca) band set into it made from small wedge parts and a row of white dots on each side; 2 large flower motifs, one on each flank (8 petals in pink, magenta, sky and cobalt around a gold centre, with a white dot ring), and smaller flowers on the shoulder and haunch; rows of tiny cream and white dots along the belly line and chest; a chest bib of cream with red and turquoise triangle points; a necklace-like band of alternating coloured beads around the chest base where the neck sprouts; a small raised ridge of leaf shapes along the backbone in leaf and lime green. Also builds the shoulder and haunch masses (large flattened spheres at x +-0.3 on the shoulders at z~0.5 and at the hips at z~-0.5, y~0.8) in jaguarOrange with indigo dot rings, so the legs read as growing out of them. Hip and shoulder masses stay inside x +-0.45.
parts.attaches: Skinned to hips, spine1, spine2 and chest. The neck sprouts at the neckBase mount (inside the chest), the wings root at wingRootL/R (just above the shoulders, covered by a flower rosette boss on each side), the tail begins at tailRoot, the legs start at the shoulder and hip mounts inside the shoulder and haunch masses.

parts.builds: The eagle head and neck. Neck: a thick tube along neck1 and neck2 from neckBase (radius ~0.2 at the base, ~0.15 at the head), cream front and jaguarOrange back sectors, with a ruff collar of 14-18 overlapping feather blades (extrude or slab) ringed around the neck base in marigold, magenta, turquoise, cobalt rotating colours, each with a white dot, and rows of small dots up the neck. Head: a strong faceted skull (about 0.34 wide, 0.32 tall, 0.4 long) centred at headCentre in jaguarOrange with a cream face mask and a turquoise brow band. The eagle beak is built in two separate pieces: an upper beak on the head joint, a hooked cone or loft in beakYellow starting at beakBase and curving down to a sharp tip at beakTip (z~1.5), with nostril dots, a dark red outline stripe, and a rawWood ridge; and a lower jaw on the jaw joint, a shorter beakYellow wedge opened slightly under the upper, with a red tongue sliver and small jaguar fangs (white cones) at the corners of the mouth. Eyes: big round forward-and-sideways facing eyes at x +-0.15 on the front of the skull (y~1.47, z~1.05): black outline disc, gold iris disc, indigo pupil, tiny white highlight, a brow ridge of heavy indigo wedge above each eye with 3 small dots, and an eyeliner swirl tail in magenta. Jaguar ears: two round ears on the top-outer skull (x +-0.15, y~1.62, z~0.88) in jaguarOrange with an indigo rim and a cream inner disc. Crest: a fan of about 9 tall feather blades rising from the crown between the ears (y 1.6..1.9, tilted backward and fanned sideways) in a rainbow of red, marigold, lime, turquoise, cobalt, violet and magenta with white tips and dot centrelines. Cheek ruffs: 3 layers of short feather blades under each cheek, and a swirl-and-dots pattern on each cheek in turquoise, white and magenta. The highest point of the model is the crest tip, y~1.9.
parts.attaches: Neck tube starts inside the chest at neckBase on neck1 and ends in the skull at headCentre; upper beak, skull and crest ride head; lower jaw rides jaw (hinge at jawHinge). The collar ruff sits over the junction of chest and neck.

parts.builds: All four legs, mirrored left and right, sweeping tubes bound to the leg joints (smooth skin or rigid capsules per bone). Front legs: jaguar forelegs, thick (radius ~0.1 at the top down to ~0.075 at the wrist), jaguarOrange with indigo spots, a magenta and cream band cuff (a ring of sweep) at the wrist with white dots, big rounded paws at pawFL/pawFR (flattened sphere, ~0.13 wide, 0.2 long, reaching z~0.78) in cream with 4 toe bumps (small spheres) and indigo claw cones pointing forward, plus a red and turquoise toe-stripe. Hind legs: fat feathered thighs (a heavy ellipsoid from hipHL/hipHR to kneeHL/kneeHR) covered with 3 rows of overlapping short feather blades in marigold, magenta and turquoise with white dots, a slim bird shin and hock sweep (radius ~0.055) in jaguarOrange with a zigzag greca ring in cobalt and white, then an eagle foot at footHL/footHR: 3 forward toes (tube segments with 2 knuckle spheres each, about 0.2 long, splayed 25 degrees) in beakYellow with rawWood scale rings, and 1 rear toe, each ending in a curved black-indigo talon cone; toe bottoms touch y=0 and pads sit about 0.05 above. Each leg also gets a couple of small flower dots on the upper leg. Lowest points of all paws and talons rest on y=0 (sink up to 0.02).
parts.attaches: The leg tops are buried in the torso's shoulder and haunch masses at shoulderFL/FR and hipHL/HR; the paw and foot tips sit at pawFL/FR and footHL/HR. All geometry rides the listed leg joints.

parts.builds: Two big eagle wings, mirrored, spread out and slightly raised from wingRootL/R to wingTipL/R at x +-1.7 (wrist y~1.45, tip y~1.5), the feather edge trailing toward -Z. Each wing: a thick arm tube along wingShoulder, wingElbow, wingWrist and wingTip (radius 0.1 tapering to 0.05) in jaguarOrange with indigo spots; a leading-edge ridge of small dots; 3 rows of feathers built as extruded blade shapes (rounded tips, each with a thin contrasting centre rachis stripe and a row of white dots): lesser coverts (about 8 short feathers, 0.2 long, cream and pink with rosettes), greater coverts (about 8, 0.3 long, turquoise, cobalt and lime), and flight feathers: about 9 secondaries from the elbow to wrist (0.7 long, each in a different colour cycling magenta, marigold, turquoise, cobalt, violet, leaf, red, sky, orange, each fading to a white-tipped feather end in a second small part) and about 6 long primaries from the wrist to tip (0.85 long, splayed like fingers, rotating through the same palette with black-indigo outline stripes and dotted cream tips). Each wing has a large flower rosette boss on the shoulder joint where it meets the torso and a zigzag band along the wing's forearm. Feather colours alternate left and right so the wings are symmetric but vivid. Keep all wing geometry above y=0.95, with feather tips reaching back to z~-0.7 and spanning x up to +-1.75.
parts.attaches: Roots at wingRootL/R above the shoulders at the sides of the torso, rigid on the wing joints (wingShoulder, wingElbow, wingWrist, wingTip). The flower boss hides the seam with the torso.

parts.builds: The tail, a jaguar tail with an eagle plume: a tube swept along tail1-4 from tailRoot (radius 0.1) tapering to 0.05 at tail4 (0,1.2,-1.8), curving back and rising, banded jaguarOrange with alternating indigo, cream and magenta ring bands (use bands or ring sweeps) and an indigo dotted spiral of spots; small turquoise zigzag segments on the upper side. At tail4 sprouts a fan of 7-9 large flame-like feather blades (extrude, 0.45-0.6 long, S-curved tips) fanning upward and backward from tail4 (tips reach z~-2.0, y up to ~1.5), in layered colours red, marigold, magenta, turquoise, cobalt, violet, lime, each with a smaller inner blade in a contrasting colour and a row of white dots, plus a rosette flower boss at the base of the plume. A small rump flower (6 petals plus gold centre) sits on the top of the tailRoot. Some thin curly vine tendrils (sweeps in leaf and lime) with small leaf shapes decorate the plume base.
parts.attaches: Starts inside the rump at tailRoot (hips/tail1 joint chain) and rides tail1 to tail4; the plume is rigid on tail4.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning the spec for an alebrije jaguar-eagle, sizing it around a jaguar body with eagle head and wings. I'm estimating a wingspan of about 3.0 m, a raised head height of roughly 1.6 m, and a length of about 2.6 m including the tail, with the wings extended in the rest pose.

Next I'm settling the placement of the limbs: forelegs as jaguar paws, hind legs with feathered thighs ending in eagle talons, and I'm weighing whether the painted pattern and the dot border around the rim should cover the whole body.

I'm breaking the model into five parts: body, head and neck, legs, wings, and tail, with a rough budget of about 900 for the whole spec. I'm now working through the head details, the legs and their painted anklets, and the wing feathers, and I'm starting to set coordinates with the body facing forward along +Z.

I'm placing the torso between the rump and the chest, with the body centred around y 0.82 and legs about 0.6 long. The neck rises from the chest top toward the eagle head, which sits near (0, 1.5, 1.0) with its beak reaching forward, and I'm starting to place the wings at the shoulders.

I'm adjusting the wing span to about 3.4 m and settling the overall bounding box at roughly 3.4 by 1.9 by 3.5 m, with the body running from z -2.0 to 1.5. Next I'm placing the hip root and the first spine joints along the centreline.

Still defining joint coordinates for the spine, neck, and tail chains.

I'm now defining the leg joints for the shoulders and elbows, with the front legs hanging down from the chest and the tail tip set at the far end of the tail chain.

I'm fixing the wing joints now: the shoulders sit at the chest and the wing chains run outward and slightly up. I'm also settling that the joint list is final, with no extra joints added by the part builders, and that the feathers stay rigid to the wing joints.

I'm settling the wing joints now: the shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip of each wing, with the primary and secondary feathers rigidly bound to the wrist and elbow.

Still placing the hind legs, with the knee and hock joints set along the back legs as I go.

I'm settling the bounding box for the torso and neck-head region, with the torso running from about x ±0.38, y 0.5 to 1.2, z -0.85 to 0.85, and the head box extending up toward y 1.9.

I'm checking the legs box against the body and settling it at about y 0 to 0.9, so the upper thighs sit inside the torso and bulge out of its sides.

I'm laying out the bounding boxes now: the wings span about x ±1.75 and reach up to y 1.85, with the feathers trailing back toward the tail. The tail box curves up behind the body, ending in a plume near z -2.0, and the head box tops out at 1.9. I'm also starting to pick the palette, with jaguar orange and marigold as the main colours.

I'm listing the palette colours, the pinks, turquoise, cobalt and so on, with gold for the beak and burnt orange for the accents. Next I'm placing the neck base and head centre, and starting on the jaw.

I'm now placing the hinge joint and beak base near the head, along with the wing roots, tail root, and the shoulder and hip joints, and checking where the feet meet the floor. I'm also deciding the pattern language for the spec: painted white-dot outlines, five-petal flower rosettes on the flanks, wings and thighs, zigzag bands and swirl vines, with each feather layer carrying its own colour.

I'm working out the head design now: an eagle head with a big hooked beak and a jaw joint, gold-ringed eyes with brow ridges, and a rainbow blade crest. I'm also considering small round jaguar ears with dotted rosettes, a red tongue and fangs, and a feather ruff collar at the neck, but I'm leaving the neck loft to the body part.

I'm now writing out the joint list in JSON, and I'm deciding the torso loft stations, with rough widths and heights at each z position so the builder has a range to work from. The neck starts inside the chest and the head box overlaps it at the base. I'm also settling the colouring: orange body with dark rosettes, cream belly with dots, a magenta saddle stripe with turquoise zigzags, and flower motifs on the flanks.

Still writing the joint list: the spine, neck, and head chains are being laid out as listed, with the jaw hanging off the head.

Still defining the tail chain and the wing joints: the tail runs back from the hips with its tip curving up, and each wing is a shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip chain running outward from the spine.

Still setting the leg joints: the front shoulder hangs down from the chest with the elbow, wrist, and paw stacked below it, and I'm making sure the paw sits just above the floor.

Still setting the hind legs: the hip, knee, and hock sit along the back leg, with the foot stacked just above the floor.

I'm now deciding what goes into each part: the body carries the back saddle, rosettes, belly dots, flank flowers and haunch ornament, while the tail gets ringed bands and a plume of seven large flame-feather blades at its tip.

I'm going to write buildLegs efficiently since the joints already exist and can't be chained over, so I'll attach a capsule between joint positions per bone instead. I'm also planning a small dot helper that takes a position, radius, color, and bone.

Still writing the leg geometry...

Still working through the leg geometry, now the spots and the hind leg: I'll scatter indigo dots along the leg path, and I'm planning the thigh as a scaled ellipsoid centered between the hip and knee.

Still working on the feather blades for the thigh: I'm weighing whether to use flattened ellipsoids tilted downward and back, scaled thin in one local axis, and I'm sorting out how the default roll affects which axis ends up as thickness.

Still working on the feather blades along the thigh, sizing them as thin plates oriented downward so their wide face points outward.

Still working on the shin, sweeping an orange tube from the knee through the hock toward the foot.

Still writing the shin ring, placing alternating cobalt and white wedge boxes around the lower leg at a fixed angle step.

Still writing the foot: I'm placing three forward toes splayed about 25 degrees, plus one rear toe, each a short capsule from a base point slightly above the ground.

Still writing the foot: I'm adding knuckle spheres and rawWood rings along each forward toe, then talon cones at the tips, with a rear toe at 180 degrees.

Still writing the foot, placing the heel pad and planning the flower dots on the upper legs.

Still writing the front leg: I'm sampling a path through shoulder, elbow, and wrist, then placing indigo spots along it, alternating which bone each one attaches to.

Still writing the front leg cuff: I'm placing two tori and a row of white dots around the wrist, using a perpendicular basis built from the leg direction.

I'm writing buildWings using the Ctx helper, aiming for something detailed but not overwhelming, and I need to be careful with the API. I'm planning each side as a mirror image, with joints for the shoulder and a swept arm path through shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip.

Still writing feather geometry...

Still working out the primary feathers: I'm placing six of them between the wrist and the tip, angled mostly backward with a small outward splay so they stay within the wing's span.

Still working out the feather layout: the coverts go over the arm line with a slight lift, and the flight feathers sit a little lower so the wing stays above the floor. I'm also adding a small white tip at the end of each feather, raised a touch so it doesn't flicker against the main shape.

Still writing the tip geometry: I'm defining a helper that builds a small tapered shape at each feather end, slightly thicker and raised a touch so it sits cleanly on the main feather.

Still working on the tip helper and the flower rosettes: I'm placing small petal spheres in a horizontal ring on the coverts, and a larger boss on top of the shoulder.

Still working out the flower helper: I'm building a manual basis perpendicular to the direction vector so the petals can be laid out in a ring.

Still writing the flower and arm detail code...

Still writing the arm details: I'm placing a zigzag of small cones along the top of the arm, alternating their tilt, and I'm about to pull the shoulder and arm joint positions from the joints table.

Still working on the arm details: I'm laying out the shoulder, elbow, and wrist as capsules with tapering radii, and placing indigo spots along each segment so they sit on top of the arm.

Still working through the budget for the feathers: the primaries get a slightly larger indigo under-feather with white dots near the tips, and the rachis dots.

Still working on the budget: I'm cutting the part count by merging the small white dots into one batched geometry per bone, since the total is running well over the limit.

Still working out the budget: I'm merging the small dots and spots into batched geometry per bone to keep the part count down, and I'm dropping the rachis on the greater coverts too.

Still working on the budget: I'm collecting the small dots and petals into merged geometry per colour and bone, so the wing stays around 85 parts each and the total fits under 230.

Still writing the feather helper: I'm defining it to take a root, direction, length, width, colour, and joint, with optional under-feather, rachis, tip, and dot settings, and building the outline as an extruded shape.

Still writing feather dots and the arm points: I'm setting dots along each feather at a few fixed fractions, sitting just above the surface, and about to pull the shoulder position from the joints for each side.

Still working on the secondary feathers along the forearm, sweeping them back toward the tip.

Still working on the primary feathers: I'm spacing six of them from the wrist toward the tip, angled backward, and giving the first four to the wrist joint and the rest to the tip joint. Each one gets a slightly larger indigo under-feather behind it.

Still working on the greater and lesser coverts: I'm placing eight of each along the arm, with the lesser ones lifted slightly, and adding small flower rosettes on top of the lesser coverts.

Still working on the boss: I'm placing a disc with petals and a white dot ring around the shoulder, with a gold centre.

Still writing the leading-edge dots and the final touches, and I'm about to finish the code.

I'm going to write one compact buildHeadNeck function that takes the Ctx destructure, relying on the module's ambient Ctx type rather than importing it. I'm planning out the coordinates carefully, placing each part with an explicit at and bone through plain b.part calls.

Still placing the skull and face parts...

Still working out the skull band: I'm checking how far the brow surface curves at that height, and settling on a flattened sphere placed at the front of the head instead of a box that might poke out.

Still writing the beak: a tapering sweep from the base to a point, with a thin ridge along the top and two small nostril dots.

Still placing the beak's lower jaw, the tongue, and the fangs, and the eyes come after that.

Still placing the eyes: each one is a stack of discs (black rim, gold ring, indigo pupil, white glint) angled outward and forward.

Still placing the eyes: each one is a small set of stacked discs, and I'm working out a thin magenta eyeliner swept back from each eye while checking that it stays clear of the skull's surface.

Still placing the ears: I'm positioning a flattened disc pair on top of the skull at either side, layering an indigo rim, an orange body, and a cream inner.

Still working out the crest: I'm laying out nine blades fanned out from the top of the head, each shaped as a tapering outline and angled backward.

Still writing the crest: I'm working out the orientation of each blade and adding a small white tip to each one.

Still building the crest blades: I'm settling on a shared helper that takes a position, a direction, a length, and a color, and I'll reuse it for the cheek ruffs too.

Still placing the ruff: I'm arranging sixteen blades around the base of the neck, angled outward and downward so they drape over the chest, and the back ones will sit close enough to the torso that they overlap it.

Still working out the cheek ruffs, fanning a second set of blades out along the sides of the face.

Still placing the cheek ruffs: three layers of three blades on each side, angled outward and down along the face. Next up is a turquoise, white, and magenta disc pattern on each cheek.

Still placing the cheek discs and neck dots: I'm setting the cheek pattern at the face's edge, then spacing small white dots up the neck, each sized to the neck's narrowing radius.

Still placing the neck dots: I'm putting small white spheres at the side angles of the neck, alternating magenta and white along the boundary.

Still writing the blade helper: I'm setting up its orientation and width so the feathers overlap cleanly.

Still writing the blade helper: I'm getting the tip shape right, a small triangle at the top that sits inside the main outline so the two overlap cleanly.

Still writing the blade helper: I'm finishing the tip so it sits just inside the main outline, and placing a white dot on each face of the blade.

Still writing the helper signatures and the eye discs: I'm setting the disc function to place each cylinder along its direction, and I'll pull the palette and mount values from the shared constants.

I'm writing the torso function, keeping it manageable but detailed. The context type comes from the module, so I'll take it as given in the destructured parameter. My plan is to loft stations along the z-axis over a bone chain running from the hips up through the spines to the chest.

Still working out the rosette placement on the belly surface...

Still working out the rosette placement, now filtering the scatter hits so they stay clear of the saddle and the flank flowers.

Still writing the flower and mass details...

Still writing the mass and dot details...

Still writing the saddle and greca details...

Still working out the saddle and greca details, looking at how to place the turquoise wedges along the back line by pairing each path point with its nearest surface hit.

Still writing the leaf ridge along the spine, placing the leaves at points on the back surface.

Still working on the leaf ridge, now shifting the leaves off the saddle to alternate along its edges, with the greca and white dots kept on the saddle itself.

Still writing the color sectors, deciding which bands of the belly and flanks get marigold and which stay cream, with white dots marking the edges.

Still writing the bib, now planning flat triangles along the chest front, each with red and turquoise points, and leaning toward extruded outlines over spiky cones.

Still writing the bib, now placing the bib's cream backing and the red and turquoise triangles on the chest front with a ray cast to find the surface, and adding a row of necklace beads around the chest base.

Still working on the necklace, now placing a ring of beads around the chest at z=0.72 with a thin indigo cord beneath, looping the beads along the path.

Still writing the necklace, now helping each bead sit on the chest surface by snapping it to the nearest hit, and looping the beads with a skin loop along the chest base.

Still working on the flowers along the flanks, placing each one by taking a surface hit at the center and then adding petals and a dark disc, with a gold center and a ring of white dots.

Still working out the scatter layout, placing rosettes as rings of indigo spheres around a gold or magenta center, and filtering out any spots that would land on the saddle or the flank flowers.

Still working out the placement filters, now excluding spots that land too close to the flank flowers, shoulders, and wing roots, while keeping the rosettes off the saddle and belly.

Still working through the rosette count, weighing the part budget against the scatter density.

Still working out the rosettes, now switching to merged geometry so each rosette costs only a couple of parts instead of one per sphere.

Now I'm counting up the parts budget for the rosettes, flowers, masses and dot rows, and it looks tight. The plan is to merge each dot row into one geometry placed at the spine bone rather than stick each dot separately.

Still writing the batching helper, grouping the dots into the bone regions by height so each group can merge into a single geometry.

Still writing the placement helper, now building each decoration as geometry in model space and orienting it to the surface normal so the pieces can be batched into fewer parts.

Still writing the bib triangles, shaping each one as a short cone turned to face forward so they can be batched with the rest.

Still writing the bib triangles, now shaping each one as a flattened three-sided cone, with its tip pointing down the chest front so it sits flush against the surface.

Still working out the bib triangles, now orienting each cone so its tip points down the chest front and flattening it so it sits flush with the surface.

Still writing the greca wedges, now looking at a flattened three-sided cone along the local axis, with its direction alternating so the row forms a zigzag along the saddle.

Still writing the batching helper, now flattening each rosette's ring and centre into local geometry, merging the pieces by bone and colour, and placing them with an orientation matrix aimed along the surface normal.

Still working out the body stations, now checking the chest's height so the top doesn't run past the box, and wondering whether the loft accepts the sector options the same way the sweep does.

Still writing the saddle, sampling points along the body line and sweeping a flattened box-section tube over them.

Still writing the saddle and greca, now placing the wedges at nearest surface hits with alternating spin, and the white dots at a fixed offset from the line.

Still writing the leaves along the spine, sizing each one as a flattened sphere and alternating their colors, with flower placement on the flanks next.

Still working out the shoulder flowers, now placing them by ray-casting onto the mass surfaces rather than the body, and ringing each one with indigo dots.

Still working out how the masses fit with the body, placing the shoulder and haunch flowers on their surfaces with rings of indigo dots around them.

Still writing the bib, now placing a few overlapping flattened spheres as the cream backing and setting a row of alternating red and turquoise cones beneath it.

Still working on the bib, now placing a row of cream discs on the chest front where the rays hit, with a line of red and turquoise triangles beneath them.

Still working on the necklace, now looping a row of colored beads around the chest base and snapping each one to the nearest surface hit.

Still writing the torso's surface details, picking dot-row positions on the belly and chest and settling on a few named colours for the decorations.

Still writing the rosette geometry, merging a ring of small spheres into one piece so each rosette stays within the parts budget.

Still writing the rosette geometry, now sketching the flower builder: petals in alternating colors around a gold centre, a dark disc beneath, and a ring of white dots.

Still writing the rosette and flower helpers, now sketching a `rayHit` function to find surface points and setting up a path sampler that pulls positions along the body line.
